transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2025-11-05
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Miller (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Mike Tanaka (CTO - Nebula Health), Ana Rodriguez (Head of ML), Samir Gupta (Platform Eng)

AUTO-SUMMARY (auto-generated): Quick Optimize walkthrough focused on quantization (INT8 vs FP8). Demo'd console views and a small benchmark. Agreed next steps: share spreadsheets, provide traffic trace, schedule pilot.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Miller: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan, AE on the Redwood side; joining me is Priya our SE. How's everyone doing?
[00:10] Mike Tanaka: Good, thanks. Appreciate you squeezing this in. We're excited to see the quantization stuff — we've read the notes but want to see how quality holds up.
[00:18] Priya Rao: Awesome. We'll do a quick agenda: 1) brief intro to quantization profiles in Redwood Optimize, 2) show INT8 vs FP8 benchmarks (latency and quality metrics), 3) console walkthrough, 4) discuss pilot scope and security. Interrupt anytime.
[00:30] Ana Rodriguez: Sounds good. For context, our main workload is real-time triage and extraction from patient notes, ~1k requests/sec at peak, p95 latency target 300ms, and accuracy on entity extraction is critical.
[00:45] Samir Gupta: And we have VPC-only requirement for PHI — so on-prem or private deploy is possible but ideally dedicated in our VPC.
[00:55] Jordan Miller: Great, that helps shape recommendations. Quick primer: in Redwood Optimize we ship curated quantization profiles. INT8 generally offers the largest cost and latency wins but can introduce small quality regressions on some models; FP8 (bfloat-like) is often a better quality/latency middle ground, especially for longer contexts.
[01:20] Priya Rao: We're going to show two example profiles we've used in similar customers: "optimized-int8-low" (aggressive, best latency) and "fp8-balanced" (safer quality with still sizeable latency wins). We'll also highlight fallback policies so production can degrade gracefully.
[01:37] Mike Tanaka: Curious — do you have empirical numbers for both short prompts and long context? our average is short but we keep 8k context windows for some workflows.
[01:46] Priya Rao: Yes, we ran benchmarks on both 2k and 8k windows. For the model family you indicated in the intake (open-llm-psi-7b equivalent), INT8 gave ~2.6x throughput increase and p50 latency drop from 220ms to ~85ms on our T4-like infra. FP8 yielded ~1.6x throughput and p50 ~140ms.
[02:10] Ana Rodriguez: And quality? our extraction F1 is non-negotiable — we need <1% delta ideally.
[02:17] Priya Rao: Right. On QA and extraction evals we saw INT8 sometimes slipped by 2-4% relative to FP32 on adversarial sets; FP8 was within 0.5-1% in most cases. But this varies by model and prompt.
[02:33] Jordan Miller: Important note — Redwood Optimize includes automatic regression monitoring tied to your eval sets. If a quantized rollout causes a regression beyond your threshold we can auto-roll back to a safer profile.
[02:45] Samir Gupta: How often do you see INT8 regressions in production customers?
[02:50] Priya Rao: It's relatively uncommon on reasoned workloads but does happen on edge cases, long-tail prompts, or models with heavy numeric precision needs. That's why pilots are important — we'll run your representative traffic through both profiles and give you per-query diffs.
[03:05] Jordan Miller: Ok, Priya will share the benchmark spreadsheet after this call. It includes token distribution, latency histograms, and per-eval set deltas.
[03:14] Mike Tanaka: Cool. Can you show the console now?
[03:17] Priya Rao: Sure. (screen share) Here's the Optimize tab — you can see "Profiles" and compare metrics side-by-side. I'm selecting Nebula-sample-run (demo data) — you'll see p50/p95, cost per 1M tokens, and a quality delta chart tied to our eval suite.
[03:35] [00:03:36] Priya Rao: Note the left panel: profile configs, quantization algorithm (symmetric vs asymmetric), per-layer override options. We've prefilled recommended layer exceptions for commonsense MLP/attention layers to avoid numerical underflow.
[03:50] Ana Rodriguez: That per-layer override — can we lock it down or do you recommend we keep it editable?
[03:55] Priya Rao: You can lock profiles in Dedicated/Private deployments. For initial pilot we usually keep them editable for iteration, then freeze a profile once it meets SLAs.
[04:05] Samir Gupta: On the dedicated side, how does KMS integration work for keys used in caching or logs? We need CMEK across the board.
[04:12] Jordan Miller: We support customer-managed keys (CMEK) and HSM options on Private deployments; Dedicated supports VPC peering and restricted egress and we can integrate with your cloud KMS. We'll attach the security playbook in the follow-up.
[04:28] Mike Tanaka: Good. Back to numbers — you said INT8 gave 2.6x throughput on T4-like infra. We're evaluating both cost and latency — can you show cost per 1M tokens?
[04:39] Priya Rao: (points at chart) For this run, FP32 baseline was ~$120 per 1M tokens. FP8 was ~$48 / 1M, INT8 ~$22 / 1M — approximate and infra-dependent. The big caveat: if INT8 requires you to fall back to FP32 for certain prompts frequently, effective cost will be higher. That's why selective per-request routing helps.
[05:05] Ana Rodriguez: For our compliance, we may need to pin to FP8 if quality risk is too high.
[05:10] Jordan Miller: Totally reasonable. FP8 is a common default for customers with strict accuracy targets.
[05:16] [00:05:17] Mike Tanaka: How do you handle mixed workloads where some calls are short chat style and some long context? Do you auto-route?
[05:23] Priya Rao: Redwood's routing can be policy-driven — e.g., route low-latency, high-importance requests to FP32 or FP8, and batchable background inference to INT8. You can also set SLOs per route.
[05:35] Samir Gupta: Our traffic is bursty. Does Optimize change batch sizes or caching settings automatically?
[05:40] Priya Rao: Yes, Optimize recommends batching and KV cache policies. In Dedicated we can tune the runtime (continuous batching thresholds and max batch size per model variant). Those recommendations are surfaced in the Console with expected unit cost impact.
[05:55] Ana Rodriguez: Any gotchas with long context (8k) and INT8?
[06:00] Priya Rao: Long contexts increase KV cache memory pressure; INT8 reduces memory but precision loss in the KV might amplify drift for certain generation tasks. In our 8k tests INT8 still had gains but we saw modest quality deltas — FP8 was safer. We'll surface per-token attention metrics in the benchmark sheet.
[06:18] Jordan Miller: I'm going to pull up the benchmark we ran with Nebula-ish prompts. (shares table) This is synthetic but approximates your token distribution.
[06:26] [00:06:27] Priya Rao: You can see per-eval line: extraction F1 baseline 0.897 (FP32), FP8 0.892, INT8 0.865 on the adversarial set. Latency p95: FP32 420ms, FP8 260ms, INT8 140ms.
[06:45] Ana Rodriguez: Those deltas on F1 for INT8 are larger than we can accept. FP8 looks promising though.
[06:51] Priya Rao: Agreed. For your use-case I'd recommend an FP8-balanced profile for the pilot and a phased test of INT8 on non-critical routes. Also set the rollback threshold to 1% F1 delta.
[07:05] Mike Tanaka: What about automated AB tests? Can we run dual runs and compare per-request diffs?
[07:11] Priya Rao: Yes, Optimize supports shadowing and per-query diff logs. We can run a 2-week shadow that records the FP32 answer and the quantized answer for offline scoring. That gives a clear picture without risking production traffic.
[07:25] Samir Gupta: How heavy is the instrumentation? We don't want to double request volume to external logs.
[07:30] Priya Rao: We provide sampling controls — you can sample 1-5% for diffs. The heavy payloads are optional; you can store diffs internally or in your S3.
[07:40] Jordan Miller: Switching gears: pilot scope. Typically we recommend: 1) share traffic trace + eval sets, 2) Redwood runs internal benchmark and provides config, 3) customer runs shadowing for 2 weeks, 4) agree on rollout profile and guardrails.
[07:55] Mike Tanaka: Timeline-wise — if we start next week, when could we move to a small pilot?
[08:00] Jordan Miller: If you share traffic trace by 11/12, we can run benchmarks and return configs by 11/14. Shadowing could start 11/18 and run two weeks. So a conservative production-ready decision by early December.
[08:15] Ana Rodriguez: That timeline works if we can get the trace and Eval sets. We'll need a short NDA addendum for pilot logging to S3 with PHI — can you send the security docs?
[08:24] Jordan Miller: Yes — Priya will attach the security and compliance playbook including SOC2/ISO attestations and KMS integration notes.
[08:31] Priya Rao: Also noting dedicated/private options — if you need dedicated GPUs in your VPC we can provision a Dedicated cluster and pre-load the quantized variants so warm-up is minimal. That helps p95 latency consistency.
[08:45] Samir Gupta: Is there a warm-up cost when switching profiles?
[08:48] Priya Rao: There's model loading and JIT/compilation overhead for some kernels; we manage version pinning to reduce cold starts. For dedicated we keep a warm pool per profile if you want guaranteed SLOs.
[08:59] Mike Tanaka: Ok, last few quick Qs: 1) Are there known model families that do poorly on INT8? 2) How do you measure perf vs cost for our billing?
[09:08] Priya Rao: 1) Some heavily quant-sensitive models (mix of older transformer blocks or models with heavy numeric tasks) can be tricky. We'll surface per-model notes in the profile. 2) Billing is per-token + per-hour reserved infra for Dedicated. Optimize shows estimated cost per 1M tokens under each profile.
[09:27] Jordan Miller: Wrap-up — recommended next steps: default to FP8-balanced for pilot, run INT8 on non-critical routes if shadowing looks good, share artifacts.
[09:36] Mike Tanaka: Sounds good. Thanks, Jordan and Priya. We'll get the trace exported by next Wednesday.
[09:41] Ana Rodriguez: One last ask — can you include example per-layer overrides you mentioned? that was helpful.
[09:46] Priya Rao: Yes — sample overrides included in the playbook.
[09:49] Jordan Miller: Alright, we'll follow up with the spreadsheet, playbook, and security docs. Thanks everyone.
[09:55] Mike Tanaka: Thanks. Bye.

End of transcript.
